turns.response_html:
It is incredibly draining when you’re just trying to optimize your workflow and instead end up 12 tabs deep in a GitHub issue thread from 2022 that doesn't even apply anymore. The Neovim ecosystem moves at a "nightly build" pace that standard LLM training cycles struggle to keep up with—especially now in 2026 with the shift toward Neovim 0.12 and the new built-in package management.

The "rabbit hole" usually happens because of a mismatch between how Neovim expects to load Lua modules and how the AI thinks they should be structured.

Why the "Snowball" Effect Happens

Most errors like E492: Not an editor command or module not found occur because of Execution Order. If your config tries to configure a plugin (like Treesitter) before the plugin manager has actually added it to the runtimepath, the whole thing collapses.

Direct Fixes for Your Recent Errors

Based on the specific "module not found" and TSInstall hurdles you've hit, here is the most stable way to bridge that gap:

1. The Treesitter "Command Not Found"

If :TSInstall fails, it’s usually because the plugin isn't "started." If you are using Lazy.nvim (the current standard), ensure your Treesitter block looks like this to force it to load correctly:

-- ~/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/treesitter.lua
return {
  "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter",
  build = ":TSUpdate",
  config = function()
    local configs = require("nvim-treesitter.configs")
    configs.setup({
      ensure_installed = { "lua", "vim", "vimdoc", "yaml" }, -- Add yaml here!
      highlight = { enable = true },
    })
  end,
}

2. Git & Cloning Failures

Since you're on a MacBook Air, Git often hangs if it's waiting for a password prompt that the Neovim UI is hiding. To stop the "access rights" snowball, run this in your terminal (Fish compatible) to use the macOS Keychain:

git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain

3. Resolving YAML Conflicts

You mentioned vim-yaml and vim-yaml-helper. In 2026, Treesitter actually handles 90% of what those older plugins used to do. If you have both, they often fight over the buffer.

  • Recommendation: Disable the standalone YAML plugins and let Treesitter + an LSP (like yamlls) handle it.

The "2026 Standard" Stack

To avoid the rabbit hole in the future, sticking to these "Golden Path" tools will make AI suggestions much more reliable, as they are the most documented:

Component2026 RecommendationWhy?
Plugin Managerlazy.nvimStill the most robust; handles the "loading order" for you.
Completionblink.cmpFast, Rust-based, and significantly easier to config than nvim-cmp.
LSP Managementmason.nvimOne-click install for LSPs, Linters, and Formatters.
Fuzzy Finderfzf-luaExtremely fast on Apple Silicon compared to Telescope.

A Tip for Prompting AI on Neovim

When asking an AI for help with Neovim, always start your prompt with:

"Using Neovim 0.11+, Lua-based config, and lazy.nvim. Provide code that fits a modular lua/plugins/ structure."

This forces the AI to ignore the mountains of outdated Vimscript advice in its head and gives you code you can actually paste.

Are you moving your config into a single init.lua right now, or are you trying to keep it modular across different files?
